title: Angles & Parallel Lines
sub: Angle types, pairs that add to 90° or 180°, and parallel lines

steps.html:
Angles

Acuteless than 90°
Rightexactly 90°
Obtusebetween 90° and 180°
Straightexactly 180°
say: Today: angles. Angles are measured in degrees. A full turn is three hundred sixty.
Smaller than ninety degrees is acute. Think: a cute little angle.
Exactly ninety is a right angle, like the corner of a book. We mark it with a small square.
Between ninety and one eighty is obtuse, wide open.
And one eighty is a straight angle: a straight line.

steps.html: An angle measures 135°. What kind is it?
say: An angle measures one thirty-five degrees. What kind of angle is it?
steps.ok: Yes! It's between 90° and 180°, so it's obtuse.
steps.okSay: Yes! It's between ninety and one eighty, so it's obtuse.
steps.no: 135° is more than 90° but less than 180°, so it's obtuse.
steps.noSay: Not quite. One thirty-five is between ninety and one eighty, so it's obtuse.

steps.html:
Angle pairs

Complementaryadd to 90° (a corner)
30° + 60°
Supplementaryadd to 180° (a straight line)
65° + 115°
Comes before S in the alphabet, and 90 comes before 180.
Complementary = Corner. Supplementary = Straight.
say: Two angle pairs have special names.
Complementary angles add up to ninety degrees, like two pieces of a corner.
Supplementary angles add up to one hundred eighty, like two pieces of a straight line.
Here's how to remember: C comes before S in the alphabet, and ninety comes before one eighty. Complementary, corner. Supplementary, straight.
What is the supplement of sixty-five degrees?
steps.ok: Yes! Supplementary means they add to 180°: 180 − 65 = 115°.
steps.okSay: Yes! Supplementary means a straight line, so one eighty minus sixty-five is one fifteen.
steps.no: Supplementary = Straight = 180°. So 180 − 65 = 115°. (25° would be the complement.)
steps.noSay: Not quite. Supplementary means straight, one eighty degrees. One eighty minus sixty-five is one fifteen.

steps.html:
When two lines cross

Across = equalvertical angles: 50° and 50°
Next to = add to 180°50° + 130° = 180°

All the way around a point = 360°.
say: When two straight lines cross, they make an X with four angles.
Angles directly across from each other are equal. They're called vertical angles.
Angles right next to each other sit on a straight line, so they add to one eighty.
And all four together, all the way around the point, add to three sixty.

steps.html: Two lines cross. One angle is 40°. What is the angle right next to it?
say: Two lines cross. One angle is forty degrees. What is the angle right next to it?
steps.ok: Yes! Neighbors sit on a straight line: 180 − 40 = 140°.
steps.okSay: Yes! Neighbors make a straight line, so one eighty minus forty is one forty.
steps.no: The angle across would be 40°. The angle next to it makes a straight line with it: 180 − 40 = 140°.
steps.noSay: Not quite. The angle across from it would be forty. But the angle next to it makes a straight line with it, so it's one eighty minus forty, one forty.

steps.html:
Parallel lines cut by a transversal

s = s = s = sall small angles are equal
B = B = B = Ball big angles are equal
small + big = 180°
say: Now parallel lines: two lines that never meet, cut by a third line called a transversal.
That makes eight angles. Sounds like a lot, but here's the secret: there are only two sizes. Small, and big.
All the small angles are equal to each other. All the big angles are equal to each other.
And one small plus one big always makes one hundred eighty degrees, because together they form a straight line.

steps.html: Parallel lines are cut by a transversal. A small angle is 70°. What is a big angle?
say: Parallel lines are cut by a transversal. One of the small angles is seventy degrees. What is one of the big angles?
steps.okSay: Yes! Small plus big is one eighty, so the big angle is one-ten.
steps.noSay: Not quite. A small angle plus a big angle is one eighty, so the big angle is one eighty minus seventy, which is one-ten.

say: Here's a tricky one. The transversal makes a ninety degree angle with the parallel lines. Find x.

steps.ask: The 90° angle and its neighbor form a straight line. The neighbor is…
steps.show: 180 − 90 = 90°. Small and big are the same size here!
steps.say: The ninety degree angle and its neighbor make a straight line. What's the neighbor?

steps.show: Every one of the 8 angles is 90°. x = 90°.

steps.html:
Bonus: shapes with more sides

triangle (3 sides): 180°
quadrilateral (4 sides): 360°
any polygon: (sides − 2) × 180°
say: One more fact, for shapes with more sides.
A triangle's angles add to one eighty. A four-sided shape, a quadrilateral, adds to three sixty, because it splits into two triangles.
For any polygon: take the number of sides, subtract two, and multiply by one eighty. A pentagon is three times one eighty, five forty.

steps.html: A quadrilateral has angles 90°, 90°, and 100°. What is the fourth angle?
say: A quadrilateral has angles of ninety, ninety, and one hundred degrees. What is the fourth angle?
steps.okSay: Yes! Three sixty minus two eighty is eighty.
steps.noSay: Not quite. A quadrilateral's angles add to three sixty. Three sixty minus two eighty is eighty.

say: Great! Now 4 practice questions. You'll see the answer and an explanation after each one.
Last part: three checkpoint questions. Get two out of three to finish the lesson. You've got this!

steps.html:
Remember

1. Acute < 90° · Right = 90° · Obtuse 90°–180° · Straight = 180°.

2. Complementary = Corner = 90°. Supplementary = Straight = 180°.

3. Crossing lines: across = equal, next to = 180°.

4. Parallel lines: only two sizes. small + big = 180°.
say: Let's review. Acute is less than ninety, right is ninety, obtuse is between ninety and one eighty, straight is one eighty.
Complementary means corner, ninety. Supplementary means straight, one eighty.
When lines cross, angles across are equal, and neighbors add to one eighty.
With parallel lines, there are only two sizes, and small plus big is one eighty. Awesome work!
